Annotate peaks with nearest gene names

Source: R/annotate-genes.R
annotate_genes.Rd

Maps significant SNPs to their nearest gene with GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest().

Usage

annotate_genes(
  data,
  genes,
  p_threshold = 5e-08,
  max_distance = 5e+05,
  top_n = NULL,
  clump_window = 1e+06
)

Arguments

data

A gwas_data object, data.frame or GRanges of variants.

genes

Gene models as a GenomicRanges::GRanges, TxDb or EnsDb object. Gene names are taken as described in gene_track().

p_threshold

Only annotate SNPs with p < this value.

max_distance

Maximum distance (bp) between a SNP and the nearest gene. The distance is 0 for a SNP inside a gene and otherwise the gap to the closest gene end. Default 500kb.

top_n

Annotate only the top N most significant SNPs.

clump_window

Clumping window in bp. Within each window, only the most significant SNP is annotated. Default 1Mb.

Value

The input as a gwas_data object with added nearest_gene and gene_distance columns.

Examples

data(example_gwas)
genes <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
  c("chr1:1000000-1500000", "chr2:50000000-51000000",
    "chr5:80000000-82000000"),
  gene_name = c("GENE_A", "GENE_B", "GENE_C")
)
annotated <- annotate_genes(example_gwas, genes, top_n = 10)
head(annotated[!is.na(annotated$nearest_gene), ])
#> Warning: no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
#> A gwas_data object: 0 variants across 0 chromosome
#>   Min p-value: Inf
#>   Lambda GC:   NA
#>   Columns:     CHR, BP, SNP, P, BETA, SE, A1, A2, AF, nearest_gene, gene_distance
